summary: JSON-LD 1.1 is the World Wide Web Consortium format for writing Linked Data, meaning facts about things and their relationships, in ordinary JSON. It covers well the naming of things by web address, the mapping of short property names to shared vocabularies through a context, and the conversion of one document between compact, expanded and flattened forms. It leaves to others every domain meaning: geometry, scenes, identity proofs, licences, networking and rendering all need a vocabulary or a separate specification layered on top. A trap for a standards audience is that a processor silently drops any property its context does not map to a web address, so two systems with different contexts can read the same file and see different data. A second is that remote contexts are fetched by address, so a document's meaning can change or fail to load unless the context is pinned or cached.

coverage.note: JSON-LD defines datatypes for values but no units of measure or real-world scale convention.
